title: "Research"
---

My research sits at the intersection of computational neuroscience and machine learning.
I investigate how intelligent systems—both biological and artificial—generalize from experience in partially observable environments.
**Highlighted research:** [arXiv:2603.27134](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.27134)

---

## Cognitive Gridworld
I developed **Cognitive Gridworld**, an open-source framework for investigating how agents learn the compositional structure of the world from naturalistic feedback.

**Resources:** [GitHub Repository](https://github.com/johnschwarcz/coggrid)

---

## Representation Classification Chains (RCC)
I designed the **Representation Classification Chains** architecture, which tackles continual meta-learning as a variational-inference problem.
The key insight was to seperate gradients for variable inference (meta-learning) and parameter estimation (continual-learning).

**Resources:** [GitHub Repository](https://github.com/johnschwarcz/rcc)

---

## Technical Toolkit & Methods

* **Core Paradigms:** Deep RL, RNNs, Variational Inference, POMDPs, Bayesian beliefs, compositional generalization, latent space.
* **Implementation:** Training and customization in PyTorch, Python scientific stack (NumPy, SciPy, Matplotlib, etc).
